text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/04/27 - Essay - 01
People exchange their views in a conversation.
Pexels · 9811867
A conversation worth having
There is more than one way to listen to a friend. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful starting
points.
One reason is that asking an open question gives the other person room to explain. For instance, we ask what happened instead of
guessing why our friend is upset. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to
notice what is happening.
Another reason is that checking our understanding prevents unnecessary disagreement. For example, we repeat the main point in our
own words before offering advice. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different
people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Identify two obstacles that could arise when people listen to a friend. Explain a workable response to each, rather than merely listing
the problems. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce
the situation; discuss asking an open question gives the other person room to explain with an example; discuss checking our
understanding prevents unnecessary disagreement with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
